name: AI-IO
summary: Learned inertial odometry for quadrotors that feeds rotor speeds alongside IMU data into a transformer velocity regressor, then fuses the predicted velocity in an uncertainty-aware EKF. Ships its own real flight dataset with IMU, rotor speed and ground truth, and also reads the DIDO dataset.
why_it_matters: The most recent open code that treats the propulsion system as a sensor: the paper (ICRA 2026) reports rotor speed improves velocity prediction accuracy by 36.9%. MIT license makes it usable for a product prototype.
hackathon_notes: Dataset is a 363 MB GitHub release asset (AI-IO_dataset.tar.gz) plus a 0.9 MB checkpoint, so it downloads in minutes. Train/eval scripts are single commands; training time and GPU need not measured here. Use its velocity output as a pseudo-measurement in an existing EKF; an IMU-only ablation gives the rotor-speed delta.

name: DIDO
summary: Code and data for Deep Inertial Quadrotor Dynamical Odometry: networks de-bias the accelerometer and gyro, learn a dynamics residual and regress velocity/position, and two EKF stages (rotation, translation) fuse them. Dataset folders hold per-sequence HDF5 files with IMU and mocap ground truth for circle and figure-eight flights.
why_it_matters: Early open example of mixing quadrotor dynamics with learned inertial estimates in a filter; its data is also the second benchmark used by AI-IO.
hackathon_notes: No LICENSE file in the repo, so reuse rights are unclear: use the data for evaluation only and ask the authors before shipping anything derived. Indoor mocap flights only.

name: VID-Fusion
summary: Visual-inertial-dynamics odometry: adds a thrust-model (from measured rotor speed) factor to a VINS-style sliding-window optimizer and estimates the external force on the multirotor together with its pose.
why_it_matters: Shows how a propulsion model enters a VIO back-end as one more factor, and gives an external-force estimate that doubles as a wind or payload signal.
hackathon_notes: GPL-3.0, ROS1 build. Needs hover data to identify the thrust coefficient. Useful as a reference design, not a 48h base.

name: VID-Dataset
summary: Visual-inertial-dynamical multirotor dataset: stereo/depth camera, hardware-timestamped IMU, commanded and measured rotor speed and motor current for all four motors, flight-controller GPS, RTK and mocap ground truth, recorded as ROS bags with a time-sync tool.
why_it_matters: One of very few open datasets with measured motor speed and current next to IMU and truth, which is exactly what a propulsion-aided estimator needs.
hackathon_notes: AGPL-3.0 on the repo. Bags are behind a NAS share link with a password listed in the README; total size not verified. Convert bags to CSV once and cache.

name: HDVIO2.0
summary: Sliding-window VIO that adds a hybrid quadrotor dynamics model (point-mass model plus learned thrust and torque residual networks fed by commands and gyro history) and estimates wind and external disturbances. Built on SVO Pro; a sample rosbag and ONNX weights are linked.
why_it_matters: State of the art (T-RO 2025) for using the vehicle's own dynamics to estimate wind while flying, which is the error term that dominates model-aided dead reckoning.
hackathon_notes: Ubuntu 20.04 + ROS Noetic + catkin. GitHub reports AGPL-3.0 while the README says GPLv3 with commercial use by contacting the authors; treat as copyleft, reference only.

name: Neural-Fly
summary: Training notebook and flight data for Neural-Fly, which learns a wind-invariant representation of quadrotor aerodynamic residual force and adapts it online. Data includes position, velocity, attitude, thrust setpoint, PWM and the computed residual force at several fan-array wind speeds.
why_it_matters: Real flight logs at labelled wind speeds with motor commands, useful to test how a drag/propulsion model degrades as wind rises.
hackathon_notes: No license file; README states personal and educational use only, written permission needed for further use. Fine for an offline wind-sensitivity plot, not for anything shipped.

name: Flight Speed Estimation Airflow
summary: GRU network that estimates multirotor flight speed from thermal anemometer readings, linked from the 2025 airflow-inertial odometry preprint.
why_it_matters: A cheap airflow sensor as a velocity source for multirotors is a rare angle; the preprint reports 5.7 m drift over a 203 s indoor flight.
hackathon_notes: MIT license but last push 2022, zero stars, needs custom hardware. Reference only.

name: TartanIMU
summary: ResNet-LSTM inertial model pretrained on more than 100 hours of car, quadruped, drone and human data that predicts body-frame velocity from 6-axis IMU, with LoRA adaptation heads, pretrained weights on Hugging Face and an IROS 2026 challenge starter kit.
why_it_matters: The first public IMU foundation model (CVPR 2025): a team can fine-tune on its own airframe instead of training from scratch.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0 code; weights license on Hugging Face not checked. The README says the public release has the LSTM model only (the Transformer core is not included). pip install -e . then run inference on a CSV of IMU samples.

name: RNIN-VIO
summary: Inertial network from RNIN-VIO (ISMAR 2021) that regresses displacement and uncertainty from IMU windows, meant to keep a VIO alive when vision fails.
why_it_matters: Shows the learned-inertial-plus-VIO coupling pattern a team would copy when the camera drops out at night or over water.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0, last push 2022, pedestrian/handheld oriented. Use as a design reference.

name: pyulog
summary: Python parser and command-line tools for PX4 ULog flight logs (to CSV, info, params, messages).
why_it_matters: The extractor for every PX4 log: ESC RPM, airspeed, wind estimate, actuator outputs and EKF innovations come out as tables for model-aided estimation experiments.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyulog; ulog2csv flight.ulg. Pairs with public logs on PX4 Flight Review. Check each log for esc_status and airspeed topics before relying on them.

name: ALFA dataset
summary: Landing page for the AIR Lab Failure and Anomaly dataset: 47 processed autonomous fixed-wing flight sequences (ArduPilot on Pixhawk) with engine and control-surface faults, plus raw bags, telemetry and Dataflash logs.
why_it_matters: Real small fixed-wing flights with full ArduPilot logs, usable to test airspeed/propulsion-aided dead reckoning against GPS truth on a real airframe, and engine-out segments test a propulsion model's failure case.
hackathon_notes: KiltHub DOI 10.1184/R1/12707963: processed.zip 272 MB, dataflash.zip 541 MB. Repository metadata says CC BY 4.0 while the bundled README says CC0, both permissive. Sequences are short (most 1-4 min). Airspeed channel presence not checked.

name: ALFA dataset tools
summary: C++, Python and MATLAB readers and evaluation helpers for the ALFA fixed-wing fault dataset, plus ROS message definitions for its bags.
why_it_matters: Saves the parsing step when using ALFA for fixed-wing navigation experiments.
hackathon_notes: No LICENSE file in the repo (the ALFA paper page calls it BSD; not confirmed in the repo). Dataflash logs can also be read with pymavlink directly.

name: Skywalker X8 simulator
summary: MATLAB simulator showcasing the Skywalker X8 flying-wing aerodynamic model from Gryte et al. (ICUAS 2018), with a basic autopilot and the coefficients in a .mat file.
why_it_matters: A published, real-airframe aerodynamic coefficient set: the process model a fixed-wing vehicle-dynamic-model navigator needs.
hackathon_notes: No license file; cite the paper. Thrust model is borrowed from the Aerosonde model per the README, so propulsion is not identified. Port the coefficients to Python rather than run MATLAB.

name: SymForce
summary: Symbolic computation and code generation library with a fast sparse nonlinear least-squares optimizer, from Skydio, which says it uses it in production for SLAM, calibration and MPC.
why_it_matters: Lets a team write a custom measurement model (drag force, rotor thrust, learned velocity) once symbolically and get optimized C++/Python residuals and Jacobians, avoiding hand-derived Jacobian bugs under time pressure.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0, pip install symforce. Learning curve is real; worth it only if the team writes new factors.

name: libRSF
summary: Ceres-based robust sensor fusion library: factor graph formulation, sliding-window filter with marginalization, and robust error models including self-tuning Gaussian mixtures for non-Gaussian, outlier-heavy measurements.
why_it_matters: The open reference for robust error models in navigation factor graphs; its GNSS datasets are reused by later integrity work (ION ITM 2026).
hackathon_notes: GPL-3.0; Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 install script. Use its datasets and ideas; for a product prototype prefer GTSAM robust kernels.

name: gnssFGO
summary: Online, time-centric factor graph optimization for GNSS and multi-sensor vehicle localization in ROS 2, with a Docker image and launch files for its Aachen data.
why_it_matters: A working ROS 2 example of an asynchronous multi-sensor factor graph where sensors arrive at different rates, the architecture behind plug-and-play fusion.
hackathon_notes: BSD-3-Clause. Archived since 2024; README says maintenance moved to the fork hz658832/gnssFGO. Docker pull is the fastest way to see it run.

name: ROAMFREE
summary: Pose-graph sensor fusion and self-calibration library on g2o with a catalogue of generic sensor models, used in UAV photogrammetry with raw inertial observations (Cucci, Skaloud).
why_it_matters: A long-lived example of a sensor-agnostic fusion library where new sensors are declared, not coded, which is the plug-and-play idea.
hackathon_notes: LGPL-3.0 per README (no SPDX on GitHub). ROS1 wrapper. Reference design.

name: ASPN-ICD
summary: Public interface control document for ASPN 2023, the All-Source Positioning and Navigation measurement message standard that grew out of the DARPA ASPN programme.
why_it_matters: Using ASPN message types for sensor inputs is a cheap way to make a hackathon fusion engine speak the plug-and-play vocabulary defence PNT programmes use.
hackathon_notes: CC-BY-4.0. Read the measurement types you need (IMU, position, velocity, altitude) and mirror them as dataclasses; no code to build.

name: pntOS-C
summary: C API specification of pntOS, the modular plug-in architecture for navigation systems that consumes ASPN-formatted data.
why_it_matters: Shows what a plug-in fusion API looks like in the defence PNT community; the full pntOS distribution is access-controlled, this API is public.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0, meson build. Headers only, no estimator inside.

name: factorGraph2DsatelliteExample
summary: Companion code to the NAVIGATION 2024 factor-graph tutorial: a simple orbit simulation and side-by-side EKF, batch factor graph and sliding-window estimators in Python.
why_it_matters: The shortest path from an EKF mindset to a factor graph, with the same problem solved both ways.
hackathon_notes: No license file. Read and port the pattern; do not ship it.

name: FGO_gnss_integrity
summary: Code behind an ION ITM 2026 paper comparing a robust factor-graph approach with solution-separation ARAIM on real GNSS epochs (from libRSF datasets) plus Monte Carlo outliers.
why_it_matters: Recent bridge between robust factor graphs and classic integrity monitoring, the comparison judges ask about when a team says 'robust kernel'.
hackathon_notes: No license file. Data DB stored via git LFS. Reference for evaluation design.

name: DEIO
summary: Learning-based event-inertial odometry: a learned event-patch front-end coupled with IMU pre-integration in a factor graph, evaluated on ten public event benchmarks.
why_it_matters: Recent open event+IMU odometry with a permissive license, the candidate if the challenge stresses high-dynamic-range or night flight.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Code uploaded 2025-07. Needs a GPU and event data (VECtor, etc.); no event camera on most hackathon rigs.

name: gr-iridium
summary: GNU Radio blocks and apps that detect and demodulate Iridium bursts from SDR recordings.
why_it_matters: The receive front-end for Iridium signals-of-opportunity experiments; burst timing and Doppler are the observables a LEO Doppler positioner needs.
hackathon_notes: No LICENSE file at the root; source headers carry GPL-3.0-or-later. Needs an SDR and L-band antenna or recorded IQ. Positioning itself is not included.

name: PyPose
summary: PyTorch library for differentiable robotics on Lie groups: IMU pre-integration, EKF/UKF modules and second-order optimizers that can sit inside a training loop.
why_it_matters: The base AirIO and AirIMU are built on; lets a team train a learned inertial or dynamics model end to end through the filter.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0, pip install pypose. Use pp.module.IMUPreintegrator to propagate and plug a learned velocity in as an EKF update.
